development_parent.diagnosis: V4 preserved a nonempty reserve through every registered outage but timed out on Object/high-jitter after 25 reserve activations and 83 hold steps. V5 retains the frozen v4 service-time and prefetch constants and changes only reserve release behavior.

phase_stability.gripper_action_convention: X-VLA LIBERO policy space: values >= +0.5 are closed; values <= -0.5 are open
phase_stability.locked_switch_rule: While the executed gripper phase is closed and the active queue is nonempty, reject a proposed backend switch and drain the already validated active queue.
phase_stability.outage_rule: Reject stale or unsafe incoming chunks without clearing a nonempty validated queue.

queue_slack_scheduler.service_observation_rule: ceil(max(request-to-delivery wall time / controller period, delivered control-step age)), clipped to [1, 28]
queue_slack_scheduler.cold_start_rule: The first observed service time is clipped to 28 steps so model warm-up cannot demand an impossible horizon.

reserve_spending.deadline_rule: At reserve activation and after each spent command, set the next release deadline to current_step + clip(predicted_service_steps - oldest_outstanding_request_age_steps, 1, 4).
reserve_spending.progress_rule: Before the deadline, release one validated reserve command when measured EEF translation is below 0.002 m and rotation is below 0.02 rad over three executed control steps.
reserve_spending.budget_rule: Spend at most four queued commands per reserve activation and never consume the final protected command. Hold the last finite absolute command when no release trigger fires or the budget/floor is exhausted.
reserve_spending.reset_rule: A replenishing accepted chunk or the absence of an unresolved request ends the activation and resets its spend budget.

capabilities.rtc_boundary: RTC remains an external official baseline; it is not relabeled as an Adaptive branch because RTC changes policy inference as well as queue merge.

claims.primary: A deterministic task-label-blind runtime that spends a bounded validated reserve when the next result misses its predicted service deadline or the measured EEF stops progressing.
non_claims: Measured EEF motion is a runtime progress signal, not task-goal progress or success prediction.
No claim of learned scheduler optimality.
No claim that canary results are a formal holdout.
No real-robot result until the separately frozen paired protocol is executed.
